input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: what exactly separates the
current Tech Preview quality of Llama Stack from the General Availability bar.
It produces the definitive GA-readiness assessment — a systematic inventory of
gaps across API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, and error handling —
consolidating TP feedback scattered across support tickets, which has never
been systematically collected. The assessment's output defines the definitive
GA scope that all Llama Stack stability and hardening work is planned against.

## Scope

- Collect and consolidate Tech Preview feedback from support tickets and other
  feedback channels relevant to Llama Stack distributions.
- Assess the current API surface (LlamaStackDistribution CRD and the
  OpenAI-compatible REST APIs exposed by the distribution) against GA stability
  expectations; inventory every gap.
- Assess upgrade behavior from the last two Tech Preview releases; inventory
  breakage and missing migration coverage.
- Assess scale limits (documented and observed) and error handling coverage
  across the distribution's surfaces.
- For each gap, record the current TP state, the GA bar, severity, and a
  recommended disposition (blocking GA vs. non-blocking).
- Produce the definitive GA scope: the consolidated, prioritized list of work
  items the graduation effort must cover, mapped to the strategy's
  requirements.
- Socialize the assessment and resulting GA scope with stakeholders for
  sign-off.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A GA-readiness assessment document exists that inventories gaps in all four
  stated dimensions (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), with each gap recording current state, GA bar, and severity.
- Every inventoried gap carries a blocking/non-blocking classification and a
  recommended disposition.
- A definitive GA scope list is produced, enumerating the concrete work items
  the graduation effort must deliver, traceable to the strategy's high-level
  requirements.
- TP feedback from support tickets is consolidated into the assessment (no
  feedback channel left unmined).
- The assessment and GA scope have been reviewed and accepted by the owning
  team and stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic is the entire
  deliverable of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and tested upgrade path

## Description

This epic puts a stability guarantee on the published Llama Stack API surface:
versioned APIs, a documented deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from
the last two Tech Preview releases. It closes the API-stability gaps that the
GA-readiness assessment identifies and delivers the technical commitments that
make the published API surface safe for enterprise customers to build production
GenAI applications against.

This epic's precise scope is defined by the GA-readiness assessment; the size
of the stability and hardening work is an estimate until that assessment lands.
If the assessment's findings change the stability work required, this epic's
scope is rewritten to match the definitive GA scope.

**Size and re-split trigger:** this epic is one logical change — the stability
guarantee on the published API surface (HLR-2's single deliverable) — so it is
not split by sub-deliverable. Its effort is unknown until the GA-readiness
assessment lands and is provisionally at the ~2-week epic guideline. Conditional
re-split trigger: if the assessment classifies the blocking API-stability gap
set as multi-sprint work, re-split this epic along the remediation vs
upgrade-path seams (gap remediation and API versioning/deprecation in one epic;
upgrade-path implementation plus its automated verification in the other).

## Scope

- Introduce API versioning for the published Llama Stack surface (the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD and the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs the
  distribution exposes), per the versioning approach selected during
  implementation.
- Author and publish a deprecation policy for the published API surface,
  including how deprecated APIs are announced and their removal timelines.
- Remediate the API-stability gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment
  (breaking changes, unstable contracts, undocumented behaviors).
- Implement a tested upgrade path from the last two Tech Preview releases,
  covering the distribution's resources and configuration.
- Add automated upgrade-path verification so migration from each of the last
  two TP releases is exercised and passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published Llama Stack API surface is versioned, and the versioning scheme
  is documented.
- A deprecation policy is published and applied: every API slated for
  deprecation is marked with an announcement and a removal timeline consistent
  with the policy.
- All API-stability gaps that the GA-readiness assessment classified as
  blocking GA are remediated or explicitly dispositioned in the GA scope.
- Automated upgrade-path verification exists and passes for migration from each
  of the last two Tech Preview releases.
- The changes build and pass the existing build pipeline for the Llama Stack
  repositories.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Published API surface carries a stability guarantee:
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases. This epic is the entire deliverable of HLR-2.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

This epic establishes the production support posture required for General
Availability of Llama Stack: documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a
supported configuration matrix. Together these artifacts tell enterprise
customers what behavior they can rely on, which releases receive fixes, and
which configurations Red Hat supports — replacing the implicit TP posture with
an explicit, published one.

The concrete SLO targets and the contents of the supported configuration matrix
are informed by the GA-readiness assessment (assessed scale limits and
error-handling gaps); this epic's deliverables are adjusted to the definitive
GA scope that the assessment produces.

## Scope

- Define and document measurable SLO targets for the GA Llama Stack
  distribution (availability and operational behavior commitments), grounded in
  the scale limits assessed during GA readiness work.
- Author the backport policy: which release trains receive fixes, for how long,
  and how security vs. functional fixes are handled.
- Author the supported configuration matrix: the provider combinations,
  versions, and deployment configurations that are tested and supported at GA
  (e.g., inference provider pairings, optional RAG vector providers).
- Remediate error-handling gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment that
  fall within the support-posture surface, so documented SLOs are backed by
  actual behavior.
- Publish the support-posture artifacts through the appropriate product
  support channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA distribution are documented, measurable, and grounded
  in assessed scale limits.
- A backport policy is documented, covering which releases receive fixes, the
  support duration, and fix-type handling.
- A supported configuration matrix is published enumerating the tested and
  supported configurations at GA.
- The support-posture artifacts have been reviewed and accepted by the support
  and product stakeholders responsible for GA commitments.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: Production support posture is in place: documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. This epic is
  the entire deliverable of HLR-3.

# TrustyAI guardrails as supported Llama Stack integration

## Description

This epic promotes the TrustyAI guardrails integration for Llama Stack
distributions from an experimental flag to a supported, documented integration.
TrustyAI already ships at GA maturity in the platform (fairness/bias metrics,
drift detection, explainability, and guardrails); the gap is that its
guardrails integration with Llama Stack is gated behind an experimental opt-in
rather than being part of the supported GA distribution surface. This epic
makes the integration supported and documented so GA customers can rely on it
for safety guardrails in production GenAI applications.

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails integration with Llama Stack distributions
  from experimental status to supported status: remove the experimental-flag
  gating for GA distributions and bring the integration onto the supported
  code path.
- Verify guardrails function correctly against Llama Stack distributions
  (enforcement on representative request flows through the distribution's
  safety surface).
- Author the integration documentation: how to enable and configure TrustyAI
  guardrails for a Llama Stack distribution, the supported scope of the
  integration, and its limitations.
- Align the integration with the TrustyAI operator's supported deployment
  model (TrustyAIService instances per data science project).

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails can be enabled for a Llama Stack distribution on the GA
  code path without any experimental opt-in flag.
- Guardrails demonstrably enforce on representative requests flowing through a
  Llama Stack distribution (functional verification passes).
- The integration is documented, covering enablement, configuration, supported
  scope, and limitations.
- The integration works within TrustyAI's supported operator deployment model
  with no experimental prerequisites.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. This epic is the
  entire deliverable of HLR-4.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic makes the Dashboard's Llama Stack management experience available by
default on entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate that
currently requires administrators to enable it explicitly. At GA, entitled
customers should see Llama Stack management in the console without any
configuration step. The Dashboard integrates with components through Kubernetes
CRs and its per-component feature flags and defaults (via the
OdhDashboardConfig CR), so this change is a Dashboard-side default/entitlement
change, not new Llama Stack surface.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement default so that it
  is on for entitled clusters, using the Dashboard's existing feature-flag and
  default mechanism.
- Implement or verify entitlement-based gating so the experience appears for
  entitled clusters and remains hidden/unchanged for non-entitled clusters.
- Verify the Llama Stack management experience (navigation section, resource
  views, status) renders and functions against Llama Stack distributions
  without any opt-in configuration.
- Update any Dashboard-internal copy or state that still labels the Llama
  Stack experience as Tech Preview opt-in (incidental to this change; no new
  content authored).

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a cluster with the relevant entitlement, the Dashboard shows Llama Stack
  management with no opt-in configuration required.
- On a cluster without the entitlement, the previous behavior is preserved
  (no regression in enablement behavior for non-entitled clusters).
- The Llama Stack management views render and function against a Llama Stack
  distribution in the default configuration.
- The Dashboard change builds and passes the Dashboard's existing build
  pipeline.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). This epic is the entire deliverable of
  HLR-5.

# Llama Stack GA documentation uplift and TP migration notes

## Description

This epic uplifts the Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and adds
migration notes for customers moving from Tech Preview releases. It runs last:
the documentation must describe what was actually built — the versioned,
stability-guaranteed API surface, the tested upgrade path from the last two TP
releases, the production support posture (SLO targets, backport policy,
supported configuration matrix), the supported TrustyAI guardrails integration,
and default Dashboard enablement on entitled clusters.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- **GA overview and support posture**: what GA means for Llama Stack
  distributions; the documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported
  configuration matrix, presented for users.
- **API stability and versioning**: the versioning scheme for the published
  API surface, the deprecation policy, and how customers should consume
  versioned APIs.
- **Migration notes from Tech Preview**: step-by-step migration guidance from
  the last two TP releases, aligned with the tested upgrade path, including
  breaking changes and required configuration updates.
- **Safety guardrails documentation**: user-facing documentation of the
  supported TrustyAI guardrails integration, referencing the integration docs
  produced by that work.
- **Getting-started and operational topics**: refresh of existing TP topics to
  GA standards, including default Dashboard availability of Llama Stack
  management on entitled clusters.
- **Removal of TP-conditional language**: retire experimental/preview caveats
  that GA status no longer excuses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covering all topics in the content outline is published and
  meets GA documentation standards.
- Migration notes from the last two TP releases are documented and consistent
  with the tested upgrade path that was implemented.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented GA
  capabilities (API versioning and deprecation policy, support posture,
  guardrails integration, Dashboard default enablement) and reflects actual
  behavior.
- No Tech Preview caveats remain in topics covered by the GA uplift.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-6 (P2)**: Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including
